newsitem.title: CANADA: Mobil Canada sees tripling output in 8 years.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Canada sees tripling output in 8 years.

text.p: Mobil Corp's Canadian unit plans to nearly triple its production over the next eight years as it pours money into east coast offshore operations and Alberta oil sands and heavy oil projects, Mobil Oil Canada president Jerry Anderson said on Wednesday.

Mobil Canada, wholly owned by the Fairfax, Virginia-based oil major, is targeting output of 325,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day by 2005, up from current production of 125,000, Anderson told reporters at a media briefing.
"We see a very positive outlook for ourselves," Anderson said.
As late as last year, Canadian industry observers speculated Mobil was in the process of pulling out of Alberta and Saskatchewan to focus solely on the east coast offshore.

The talk started about 18 months ago when the company said it would no longer be a player in high-risk western Canadian oil and gas exploration and intensified when it spun off about C$300 million worth of non-core properties into a royalty trust last year.
"I can assure you that's far from the truth. In fact, we're growing our production in western Canada," Anderson said.
Company plans include keeping light oil and gas liquids production flat, increasing natural gas output by 10 percent per year and bolstering heavy oil production with two big projects.
Mobil said in April it was studying a C$1-billion oil sands mining and bitumen extraction project in Alberta's Athabasca region which could begin producing 100,000 barrels a day in 2003.

Anderson also said a steam-assisted gravity drainage heavy oil project at Celtic in northwestern Saskatchewan, where a test operation is now producing 7,000 barrels a day, could eventually become a 50,000 to 80,000 barrel a day operation if economics proved favorable.

On the east coast, Mobil Canada expects to yield net production from the Hibernia, Terra Nova and Sable Island projects of 100,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2000, he said. Mobil Canada is a dominant player in the burgeoning offshore oil and gas region.
In 1997, Mobil Canada plans to spend a total of US$450 million on its projects, including US$140 million in western Canada and the remainder on the east coast.
That would be up from US$380 million in 1996, when US$120 million was spent in western Canada and US$260 was spent on the east coast. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
